notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0612.tlg001.perseus-: The sentence continues reported speech ('they say that...'); the subject of 'kept company' is Zoroaster, from the preceding section.

nodes.text: and that afterwards he kept company not with everyone, but with those best suited by nature to truth and able to understand the god, whom the Persians called Magi — men who knew how to serve the divine power, not as the Greeks, in ignorance of the name, use this name for wizards. These men do all other things according to sacred teachings, and in particular they keep for Zeus a chariot of Nisaean horses — these are the finest and largest in Asia — and for the Sun a single horse.
